title: The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship
program_type: Donated private-sector university scholarship considered automatically through the NUS undergraduate admission application
funding_type: Full subsidised tuition coverage + annual living and accommodation allowances and one-off allowances (donor-funded private-sector scholarship with an MOE Tuition Grant bond)
administering_authority: National University of Singapore (NUS), Office of Admissions — administering the Dr Goh Keng Swee Scholarship Fund endowed by The Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS)
implementing_agency: NUS Office of Admissions (shortlisting, selection interviews and award administration on behalf of the Dr Goh Keng Swee Scholarship Fund / ABS)
programme_action: Dr Goh Keng Swee Scholarship (GKSS) — ABS-endowed private-sector scholarship moved to single-institution administration by NUS from 2026
description: The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship is a private-sector endowed scholarship established in 1993 by The Association of Banks in Singapore (ABS) to honour the late Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Dr Goh Keng Swee. From 2026 the Dr Goh Keng Swee Scholarship (GKSS) is administered by the National University of Singapore (NUS) under its new name, The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship, replacing the earlier arrangement in which ABS awarded the scholarship across NUS, NTU, SMU and SUTD. The award is offered to outstanding freshmen from 15 Asia-Pacific economies who are applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS, excluding Dentistry, Medicine and Music. There is no separate scholarship application: all eligible students applying for undergraduate admission to NUS are considered automatically, and only shortlisted applicants are invited by e-mail to a selection interview conducted between January and July.

programme_structure.award_types: Single donated endowed scholarship (renamed and consolidated under NUS administration from 2026)
programme_structure.award_types_detail: NUS lists the award as a 'University-Level' scholarship for 'International Students' of 'Student Type: Freshmen'. The NUS List of Named Scholarships records that the ABS-GKS Scholarship was established in 2026 by The Association of Banks in Singapore with a donation of S$10.8 million.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Renewed every semester provided the scholarship recipient maintains a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and has good conduct.
programme_structure.intake: Annual. Consideration is tied to the single annual NUS undergraduate admissions application window; NUS states there is only one application window each year. Selection interviews run January to July, with outcomes by mid-July, ahead of the August (Semester 1) intake.

status_label: Next cycle (AY2027/2028) — consideration opens with the NUS admissions window on 16 December 2026
status_note: The AY2026/2027 cycle has concluded: NUS ran selection interviews from January to July 2026 and notified interviewed candidates of outcomes by mid-July 2026. As of 2026-10-03 the next cycle is not yet open — NUS's most recent admissions announcement is still the AY2026/2027 exercise, and the AY2027/2028 admissions windows published on the NUS Important Dates page open on 16 December 2026 (16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027 for International Qualifications except IB Diploma; 16 December 2026 to 3 February 2027 for the IB Diploma). The award is expected to be re-offered for AY2027/2028, subject to NUS publishing the next-cycle details.
verification_type: Direct verification against the official NUS award page and supporting official NUS, ABS and MOE pages
verified_by: ScholarZone research agent — bachelor's queue, target 50 (Singapore)
verification_notes: The official NUS award page (nus.edu.sg/oam/.../the-association-of-banks-in-singapore---goh-keng-swee-scholarship) was read and confirmed the 2026 renaming, the 15 eligible Asia-Pacific economies, the exclusion of Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents, the exclusion of Dentistry/Medicine/Music, the ban on transfer applicants, the full benefit list (100% subsidised tuition, S$6,000 annual living allowance, S$1,750 one-time computer allowance, S$5,000 annual accommodation allowance, S$200 one-time settling-in allowance, S$400 incoming and S$800 return travel allowance subject to proof of employment), the semester renewal rule (GPA at least 3.50 and good conduct), the MOE Tuition Grant requirement and its three-year bond, the no-concurrent-award rule, the repayment-on-termination rule, the automatic-consideration rule, and the January-to-July interview window with mid-July outcomes. The NUS Important Dates table independently confirms that the award has no separate application period ('Based on admissions application timeline') and that all eligible students are considered through their NUS undergraduate admission application. nus.edu.sg is protected by an Imperva/Incapsula bot challenge, so page text was obtained through a search engine's live crawl of the official nus.edu.sg URLs; every quoted string in this record comes from an official nus.edu.sg, abs.org.sg or moe.gov.sg page. No logo asset could be verified (see image.logo_verification_method).

application_deadline.typical_application_window: No separate scholarship application window exists. Consideration follows the single annual NUS undergraduate admissions window. For the cycle just completed (AY2026/2027), the International Qualifications exercise ran from 3 December 2025, 12pm to 23 February 2026. For the next cycle (AY2027/2028), the NUS Important Dates page publishes 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027 for International Qualifications (except IB Diploma) and 16 December 2026 to 3 February 2027 for the IB Diploma, with a late-application window of 18 February 2027 (late afternoon) to 19 March 2027.
application_deadline.application_period: None published for the scholarship itself. The NUS Important Dates and Application table gives the Application Period for The Association of Banks in Singapore - Goh Keng Swee Scholarship as 'Based on admissions application timeline' and states: 'All eligible students will be considered for the scholarship through their application for undergraduate admission to NUS.'
application_deadline.official_rule: NUS: 'All eligible students applying for undergraduate admission to NUS will be considered for this scholarship.' The ABS donor page likewise states: 'There is no separate application for the Dr G KS Scholarship from 2026.' Applicants must therefore meet the NUS undergraduate admissions application closing date for their qualification group; missing it means the scholarship cannot be considered for that intake.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: The official scholarship page does not publish an exact scholarship deadline date. Do not substitute a third-party date. Because consideration is automatic on the admissions application, a missed NUS admissions closing date is fatal for that intake — there is no later scholarship window to catch.

programme_duration.official_range: Tenable for the normal candidature period of the full-time undergraduate programme at NUS. The donor body ABS states the scholarship supports a maximum of four years of full-time undergraduate study at NUS (may include Honours), and NUS states Concurrent Degree Programme students are covered for the undergraduate programme for up to four years.
programme_duration.renewal_note: Renewed every semester provided the scholarship recipient maintains a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least 3.50 (or equivalent), and has good conduct.

funding.scholarship_type: Full donor-funded private-sector scholarship (tuition fee coverage plus fixed allowances)
funding.monthly_amount_note: The official page publishes an ANNUAL living allowance of S$6,000, not a monthly amount. No monthly stipend figure is stated.
funding.travel_amount_note: S$400 travel allowance to defray transport cost for incoming passage from home country to Singapore at the start of programme, and S$800 travel allowance for return passage between Singapore and home country after the completion of programme (subject to proof of employment).
funding.fully_funded_note: The award covers 100% of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees plus S$6,000 p.a. living allowance, S$5,000 p.a. accommodation allowance, S$1,750 one-time computer allowance and S$200 one-time settling-in allowance. It is NOT unconditionally 'free': recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant, which carries a three-year bond to work for a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation; renewal each semester requires a GPA of at least 3.50 and good conduct; and NUS reserves the right to impose repayment of all scholarship monies disbursed if the scholar withdraws or terminates the scholarship prematurely.

tuition.conditions: Coverage applies after the MOE Tuition Grant — scholarship recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant. For Concurrent Degree Programme students, coverage applies only to the undergraduate programme (up to the NUS subsidised undergraduate tuition fee rate) for up to four years. Fees beyond the normal candidature period are non-subsidised.

monthly_stipend.note: Not published in official source. The official page publishes an annual living allowance of S$6,000.

travel_allowance.conditions: S$400 to defray transport cost for the incoming passage from home country to Singapore at the start of programme; S$800 for the return passage between Singapore and home country after completion of programme, subject to proof of employment.

bond.conditions: MOE Tuition Grant bond: students are required to take up the MOE Tuition Grant to receive the scholarship. Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who take up the MOE Tuition Grant are bonded under the terms of the Tuition Grant — to work for a Singapore-registered company for three years immediately after graduation. NUS does not guarantee and/or provide scholarship recipients with employment upon graduation. Separately, the donor body ABS describes the underlying Dr GKS Scholarship bond as three years' work in a company in Singapore or in an approved Singapore-based company in the scholar's home country, which ABS states can be served concurrently with the MOE Tuition Grant bond; NUS's award page does not itself restate a separate ABS bond.

total_estimated_value.note: Not published in official source. NUS publishes no total award value, and no total has been computed here, per the schema rule against presenting a computed total as an award.

coverage: 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees (after MOE Tuition Grant)
S$200 one-time settling-in allowance upon enrolment
S$400 incoming travel allowance (home country to Singapore at the start of programme)
S$800 return travel allowance (Singapore to home country after completion of programme, subject to proof of employment)
coverage_limitations: Tuition coverage is 100% of the SUBSIDISED fee only, after the MOE Tuition Grant; scholarship recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant.
Scholarship recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance without prior approval from the University.

Only the tuition fee is listed as covered by NUS; compulsory miscellaneous fees (registration, student activity, health service and insurance, academic-related fees) and all living costs beyond the stated allowances are not covered.
Excluding Dentistry, Medicine and Music degree programmes.

The scholarship is tenable for the normal candidature period and covers only the undergraduate programme (up to the NUS subsidised undergraduate tuition fee rate) for up to four years for Concurrent Degree Programme students.
Does not cover students in the Concurrent Degree Programme in NUS Bachelor of Science and University of Melbourne Doctor of Veterinary Medicine.
The scholarship cannot be transferred across Dentistry, Law, Medicine or Music programmes (although it can be transferred across other programmes).
Transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible.
NUS does not guarantee and/or provide scholarship recipients with employment upon graduation.
The MOE Tuition Grant bond (three years' work in a Singapore-registered company immediately after graduation) applies to all recipients because acceptance of the MOE Tuition Grant is mandatory.

Exact benefit structure may differ from the figures published for the renamed award in its first cycle (from 2026); allowance amounts are those published by NUS for the newly named award and may be revised in future cycles.
eligible_applicants: Citizens of Brunei, Cambodia, China, Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam
Applicants applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS (freshmen / incoming students)
Applicants with strong leadership qualities and potential, a good co-curricular activities record and outstanding high school results
Applicants who are not already studying at NUS and are not transfer applicants from local or overseas universities
final_year_condition: Not applicable in the bachelor's sense — this is an undergraduate-entry (freshmen) award, and NUS's academic criterion is 'possess outstanding high school results'. Final-year secondary-school students apply through their qualification group's admissions window and must submit results as NUS requires (for example, updating and submitting actual results within three calendar days of release for AP, Gaokao, HKDSE, Indian Standard 12 and STPM, or authorising the IB to release the Diploma transcript to NUS by the published date).
equivalent_degree_note: NUS admits applicants presenting international school-leaving qualifications (for example Indian Standard 12, A-Level, American High School Diploma, HKDSE, IB Diploma, Gaokao and STPM, among others), so equivalent secondary-school qualifications are accepted for admission and therefore for scholarship consideration. Applicants who already hold a bachelor's degree or higher should note that MOE Tuition Grant eligibility depends on how the earlier degree was funded, per the NUS Registrar's Eligibility Guidelines for the MOE Tuition Grant.
nationality_quota: No per-country quota is published by NUS for this award; eligibility is limited to the 15 listed Asia-Pacific economies and to NUS admission. The donor body ABS states that 3 to 4 scholarships are awarded each year.

eligibility.citizenship: Citizens of Brunei, Cambodia, China, Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand or Vietnam. Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents are NOT eligible to be considered for the scholarship.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement is published. Applicants must be applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Yes — applicants must possess outstanding high school results and must meet NUS undergraduate admission requirements for the qualification they apply with.
eligibility.academic_requirements: No fixed minimum grade, percentage or rank is published for the award. The stated academic criterion is 'outstanding high school results'; NUS assesses the strength of the applicant's admission application.
eligibility.language_requirement: No English test or minimum score is specified on the official scholarship page. Applicants must satisfy NUS's general admission requirements for their qualification, which include English-language proficiency expectations set per qualification.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Yes — 'Have strong leadership qualities and potential'.
eligibility.financial_need: No. No means test is published for this scholarship; selection is on academic merit, leadership and co-curricular record.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Scholarship recipients may not concurrently hold any other scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance without prior approval from the University.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Freshmen (incoming students) applying for a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS. Applicants must not already be studying at NUS, and transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible.
eligibility.health_requirement: No scholarship-specific health requirement is published. All NUS undergraduates are subject to the University's standard pre-admission medical examination requirements.
eligibility.field_restrictions: All full-time undergraduate degree programmes at NUS EXCEPT Dentistry, Medicine and Music. Additionally, the scholarship cannot be transferred across Dentistry, Law, Medicine or Music programmes.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No fixed percentage, minimum grade or minimum rank is published by NUS for this award.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Applicants must meet NUS's admission requirements for the qualification applied with and the programme prerequisites of the chosen programme. NUS admissions notes that applicants completing Indian Standard 12 in the year of admission are not eligible to apply for Dentistry, Law, Medicine and Nursing — separately, this scholarship itself excludes Dentistry, Medicine and Music. Applicants without actual results may be required to submit standardised test scores for admissions consideration.
selection_factors_may_include: Strength of the NUS admission application
Performance in the scholarship selection interview (if shortlisted)
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: NUS states that invited applicants will be assessed for scholarship suitability based on the strength of their application. Shortlisting is by invitation only — only applicants shortlisted for the selection interview(s) are informed by e-mail, and interviewed candidates are informed of outcomes by mid-July.

english_requirement.test_score_note: The official scholarship page publishes no English test requirement and no minimum scores. English-language requirements are set by NUS's undergraduate admission requirements for the applicant's qualification, not by this scholarship.

language_of_instruction.language_note: NUS undergraduate programmes are taught in English (faculties offer language elective modules, but instruction is in English). The official scholarship page does not address language of instruction.

application_method.application_route: Apply for undergraduate admission to NUS via the NUS Applicant Portal (myaces.nus.edu.sg/applicantPortal). There is NO separate scholarship application from 2026 — all eligible students applying for undergraduate admission to NUS are automatically considered for The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship.
application_steps: Check the NUS Important Dates page for the application window applicable to your qualification group and confirm you meet the admission requirements and programme prerequisites.

Submit the online NUS undergraduate admission application via the Applicant Portal, upload the supporting documents listed in the Application Guide, and pay the non-refundable application fee by the closing date.
No separate scholarship application: eligible applicants are automatically considered for The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship.
If shortlisted, you will be notified by e-mail and assessed on the strength of your application; only shortlisted applicants are informed.
Attend the scholarship selection interview if invited (conducted between January and July); applications may be withdrawn if shortlisted applicants cannot attend without valid reason.

Receive the scholarship outcome (interviewed candidates are informed by mid-July) and accept the admission offer, and the scholarship offer if made, via the Applicant Portal by the stipulated deadline.
application_method.application_fee: A non-refundable application fee of S$20 for International Students with International Qualifications (S$10 for all other applicants), inclusive of prevailing GST, is charged for each NUS undergraduate application (except Music). Payment must be made by the application closing date via Visa, Mastercard, AMEX, AliPay or PayNow on the Applicant Portal. This fee is not waived by the scholarship.

official_application_documents.universal_documents: None specific to the scholarship — there is no separate scholarship application and no scholarship-specific document list. Consideration is based on the NUS undergraduate admission application.
official_application_documents.commonly_requested_documents: Documents required for the NUS undergraduate admission application as listed in the NUS Undergraduate Admissions Application Guide (International Qualifications): education details and school results for the qualification applied with, supporting documents for the chosen qualification, and achievements / short-response answers within the application form.
official_application_documents.secondary_school_documents: Yes — outstanding high school results are required. Applicants submit the supporting documents listed in the Application Guide for their qualification; applicants without actual results may be required to submit standardised test scores.
official_application_documents.document_language: Not published for this scholarship. The NUS admissions application and its supporting documents are submitted in English.
official_application_documents.document_format: Online, through the NUS Applicant Portal.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: School results / academic transcripts for the qualification applied with, per NUS admission requirements for that qualification.
official_application_documents.certified_translation_requirement: Not published for this award on the official scholarship page; refer to the NUS Undergraduate Admissions Application Guide for the documents required for the applicant's qualification.

identity_documents.requirement: Not listed on the official scholarship page; required as part of the NUS undergraduate admission application for international-qualification applicants.

academic_documents.item: High school results / academic transcripts for the qualification applied with
academic_documents.requirement: NUS criterion: 'Possess outstanding high school results' and meet NUS admission requirements for the qualification. Submit the supporting documents listed in the Application Guide.

Applicants without actual results must submit standardised test scores for admissions consideration; applicants taking AP, Gaokao, HKDSE, Indian Standard 12 (CBSE/ISC) or STPM must update and submit actual results within 3 calendar days of release.

language_documents.requirement: No English test or score is specified on the official scholarship page. Satisfy the NUS admission requirements for the qualification applied with.

recommendation_documents.requirement: NOT required for this award. NUS's own scholarship schemes (for example the NUS Undergraduate Scholarship for Singapore Citizens) require one Referee Recommendation Form, but no such requirement is listed for The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship.

application_essays.requirement: Completed within the NUS undergraduate admission application form. No scholarship-specific essay, motivation letter or personal statement is listed for this award.

financial_documents.requirement: Captured within the NUS undergraduate admission application form (may be updated before the closing date). The scholarship is not means-tested, so no financial documents or income proof are required for the award itself.

additional_documents.requirement: NUS criterion: 'Have good co-curricular activities record'. No separate CCA document submission is listed for this award; it is assessed from the admission application.

Required to claim the S$800 return travel allowance between Singapore and home country after completion of the programme (the official page states the return allowance is subject to proof of employment).

required_documents: NUS undergraduate admission application submitted via the Applicant Portal (no separate scholarship application form is required from 2026)
Academic results / transcripts and supporting documents for the qualification applied with, as listed in the NUS Undergraduate Admissions Application Guide
Standardised test scores where required by NUS admissions for the qualification applied with
Achievements and short-response answers completed within the NUS admission application form

selection_process.weighting_note: NUS publishes no weighting scheme or scoring rubric for this award. Assessment is described holistically as being based on the strength of the applicant's application.
selection_process.results_timing: Selection interview(s) will be conducted from January to July, and interviewed candidates will be informed of the scholarship outcomes by mid-July. Only applicants shortlisted for the selection interview(s) will be informed via e-mail.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: No ranking, tiering or precedence over other NUS scholarships is published for this award.

additional_factors: NUS's stated eligibility criteria are: strong leadership qualities and potential; good co-curricular activities record; outstanding high school results.
Applying for admission to a full-time undergraduate degree programme at NUS, excluding Dentistry, Medicine and Music.
Must not be a transfer applicant from a local or overseas university, and must not already be studying at NUS.
Community service is not named separately; it falls within the 'good co-curricular activities record' criterion.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree awarded by the National University of Singapore (this award is a scholarship, not a separate qualification)
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: Varies by NUS programme; the award supports a maximum of four years of full-time undergraduate study, which may include Honours
possible_awards: Concurrent Degree Programme (undergraduate portion only, for up to four years)
degree_outcome.degree_note: The scholarship is awarded to freshmen pursuing a full-time undergraduate programme at NUS. It also covers students in Double Degree and Joint Degree Programmes, and covers only the undergraduate programme (up to the NUS subsidised undergraduate tuition fee rate) for up to four years for students in Concurrent Degree Programmes. It does not cover students in the Concurrent Degree Programme in NUS Bachelor of Science and University of Melbourne Doctor of Veterinary Medicine. The scholarship is tenable for the normal candidature period and can be transferred across programmes, excluding Dentistry, Law, Medicine and Music.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Not applicable — transfer applicants from local or overseas universities are not eligible.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: 100% coverage of subsidised undergraduate tuition fees after the MOE Tuition Grant. Recipients must take up the MOE Tuition Grant. Tuition fees beyond the normal candidature period are non-subsidised and payable by the student.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: The NUS undergraduate application fee (S$20 for international students with international qualifications; S$10 for all other applicants) is payable by every applicant and is not waived by this scholarship.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Recipients must apply for and sign the MOE Tuition Grant Agreement via the MOE Tuition Grant and Scholarships portal. NUS states that incoming international students who are offered and have accepted the MOE Tuition Grant complete the application and signing in September (Semester 1) or February (Semester 2).
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Not published for this scholarship. NUS provides its standard student services to all undergraduates; the award page states no additional service entitlement.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: Yes. Students are required to take up the MOE Tuition Grant to receive the scholarship. Singapore Permanent Residents and international students who take up the MOE Tuition Grant are bonded under the terms of the Tuition Grant — to work for a Singapore-registered company for three years immediately after graduation. NUS does not guarantee and/or provide scholarship recipients with employment upon graduation. The donor body ABS additionally describes a Dr GKS Scholarship bond of three years' work in a company in Singapore or in an approved Singapore-based company in the scholar's home country, which ABS states may be served concurrently with the MOE Tuition Grant bond; NUS's award page does not restate a separate ABS bond.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Not published in detail on the NUS award page. Under the MOE Tuition Grant scheme, bond serving and deferment (including the Banker's Guarantee) are governed by MOE's Tuition Grant Scheme — Bond matters page and the TG Agreement. Separately, NUS states that if the scholarship recipient decides to withdraw from the University and/or terminate the scholarship prematurely, the University reserves the right to impose repayment of all scholarship monies disbursed to the scholar.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of one of the 15 listed economies (Brunei, Cambodia, China, Hong Kong SAR, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam) and NOT a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident
Confirm your chosen NUS programme is not Dentistry, Medicine or Music
Check the NUS Important Dates page for your qualification group's application window (the AY2027/2028 International Qualifications window opens 16 December 2026)
Confirm you meet NUS admission requirements and programme prerequisites for your chosen programmes
Prepare school results, standardised test scores (if required) and the supporting documents listed in the Application Guide
Prepare the S$20 application fee payment (international students with international qualifications)
Ensure you can be available for a selection interview between January and July if shortlisted
Understand and accept the MOE Tuition Grant three-year bond and the semester renewal GPA requirement of 3.50
Ensure you are not currently holding another scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance
programme_comparison_fields: Tuition coverage (100% of subsidised fees after MOE Tuition Grant)
Travel allowances (S$400 incoming / S$800 return, subject to proof of employment)
Bond length and type (three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond)
Renewal threshold (semester GPA of at least 3.50 with good conduct)
Whether a separate application is required (none, from 2026)
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: No scholarship essay, motivation letter or personal statement is required or listed for this award — there is no separate scholarship application from 2026. Effort should instead go into the NUS admission application itself: the achievements section and short-response answers, a coherent account of leadership and co-curricular involvement, and a clear programme choice rationale. If shortlisted, prepare for the selection interview by being able to discuss your leadership record, co-curricular involvement and reasons for choosing NUS specifically; NUS states shortlisted applicants are assessed on the strength of their application.
common_mistakes: Assuming Singapore Citizens or Singapore Permanent Residents can apply — they are explicitly not eligible
Applying to Dentistry, Medicine or Music — these programmes are excluded
Assuming a separate scholarship application form exists — from 2026 there is none, and consideration follows the NUS admissions application
Missing the NUS admissions closing date and assuming a later scholarship window exists — there is a single annual admissions application window
Expecting feedback if not shortlisted — only shortlisted applicants are informed, by e-mail
Underestimating the three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond and assuming NUS will place you in a job (it does not guarantee employment)
Ignoring the semester renewal condition (GPA of at least 3.50 and good conduct)
Planning to hold another scholarship, fellowship, bursary, grant, award or allowance concurrently without prior University approval
Applying as a transfer applicant from a local or overseas university
Relying on third-party websites that still describe the pre-2026 multi-university (NUS/NTU/SMU/SUTD) ABS application and the PSC Gateway portal

risk_flags.risk: Mandatory three-year MOE Tuition Grant bond
risk_flags.impact: Recipients must work for a Singapore-registered company for three years immediately after graduation. Applicants who intend to pursue postgraduate study immediately, or to work outside Singapore, face restricted options and possible financial consequences.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the bond as a planning constraint before applying. Read MOE's Tuition Grant Scheme — Bond matters page and the TG Agreement to understand deferment and the Banker's Guarantee requirements. ABS states its own bond may be served concurrently with the MOE Tuition Grant bond.

risk_flags.impact: The scholarship is renewed only if the recipient maintains a GPA of at least 3.50 (or equivalent) and has good conduct. A single weak semester can put the award at risk.
risk_flags.mitigation: Plan a realistic course load and use NUS academic support and advising services from the first semester. Confirm the exact consequences of failing to meet the renewal criteria with the NUS Office of Admissions before accepting.

risk_flags.impact: Only applicants shortlisted for the selection interview are informed by e-mail. Applicants who are not shortlisted receive no outcome notification and cannot tell whether they were considered.
risk_flags.mitigation: Do not wait for this scholarship. Apply for financial aid, other NUS scholarships and external options, and treat the award as an upside outcome of the admissions application.

risk_flags.impact: ABS describes 3 to 4 scholarships being awarded each year to candidates drawn from 15 economies, so per-country selection is extremely competitive.
risk_flags.mitigation: Build a broad funding plan across NUS admission, NUS financial aid, faculty scholarships and external awards. Do not rely on this award to make an NUS degree affordable.

risk_flags.impact: There is no separate scholarship application window from 2026, so applicants may assume they can apply later. Missing the single annual NUS admissions closing date eliminates scholarship consideration for that intake.
risk_flags.mitigation: Track the NUS Important Dates page for your qualification group and complete both the application and the application fee payment before the closing date. Re-verify the record before each cycle.

risk_flags.risk: Recent renaming and consolidation of the award (2026)
risk_flags.impact: From 2026 the award was renamed and consolidated under NUS, replacing the previous ABS-run scheme across NUS, NTU, SMU and SUTD. Much third-party information, including references to the PSC Gateway application route and to the SAT, is now out of date, and benefit amounts could be revised in future cycles.
risk_flags.mitigation: Rely only on the official nus.edu.sg award page and abs.org.sg. Re-verify benefit amounts, the eligible-economy list and the interview window before each cycle; this record is set for re-verification on 2026-12-20.

risk_flags.impact: NUS reserves the right to impose repayment of all scholarship monies disbursed if the recipient withdraws from the University or terminates the scholarship prematurely.
risk_flags.mitigation: Understand the termination and repayment terms before accepting, and contact the NUS Office of Admissions about documented hardship or deferral options before taking any decision to withdraw.

risk_flags.impact: The scholarship excludes Dentistry, Medicine and Music, cannot be transferred across Dentistry, Law, Medicine or Music, and does not cover the Concurrent Degree Programme in NUS BSc and University of Melbourne DVM.

image.logo_verification_method: Could not verify a logo asset URL on nus.edu.sg, so logo_url is null (an accepted honest outcome). The official NUS Identity brand guidelines pages were read (https://nus.edu.sg/identity/guidelines/logo-guideline and https://www.nus.edu.sg/identity/elements-of-the-nus-logo), which confirm that the NUS logo comprises the modernised coat of arms and the NUS namestyle, but NUS delivers logo downloads only to staff behind a login. Direct probes for logo, image and favicon assets on nus.edu.sg (nus.edu.sg/favicon.ico, /apple-touch-icon.png, /images/default-source/default-album/nus-logo.png, /oam/images/default-source/nus-logo.png) were all blocked by the site's Imperva/Incapsula bot-protection challenge and returned HTTP 200 with a 200-850 byte HTML challenge page rather than an image, so no logo file URL could be confirmed. No logo was taken from third-party aggregators, brand sites or stock sites (brandfetch.io, seeklogo.com, cleanpng.com and logo.wine were all rejected), and no logo belonging to a different awarding body was substituted for the NUS or ABS mark.

database_notes: No substitution was required. The assigned target, The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship, is not on the DO-NOT-DUPLICATE list (which contains only the NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship and the NTU Nanyang Global Scholarship for Singapore), and it is a bachelor's-level, degree-completing award hosted in an allowed region.

Official award name verified as 'The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship' (en dash between 'Singapore' and 'Goh'). NUS states: 'From 2026, the National University of Singapore will administer the GKSS under its new name, The Association of Banks in Singapore – Goh Keng Swee Scholarship.' Legacy names retained in legacy_titles are the Dr Goh Keng Swee Scholarship (GKSS), the Dr Goh Keng Swee (GKS) Scholarship, and the 'ABS-GKS Scholarship' short form used by NUS in its List of Named Scholarships.

All 13 official-source accesses were performed. nus.edu.sg is protected by an Imperva/Incapsula bot challenge that blocks direct fetching (Invoke-WebRequest and curl both return a 200-850 byte HTML challenge page, and a headless browser session was also blocked). Page text was therefore obtained through a search engine's live crawl of the official nus.edu.sg URLs, and through accessible official pages on abs.org.sg and moe.gov.sg. Every quotation in this record is traceable to an official nus.edu.sg, abs.org.sg or moe.gov.sg page.

Symlink note: the award page is reachable both under 'scholarships-for-freshmen-(international-students)' and 'scholarships-for-freshmen-international-students' (parentheses in the canonical URL). Both variants were checked and return the same content.

Bond treatment: the NUS award page states only the MOE Tuition Grant bond (three years in a Singapore-registered company). ABS's own page describes an additional Dr GKS Scholarship bond of three years in a company in Singapore or an approved Singapore-based company in the home country, which ABS says can be served concurrently with the MOE Tuition Grant bond. Both are recorded; the record flags that NUS does not restate the ABS bond, so the exact post-2026 bond architecture should be confirmed with the NUS Office of Admissions.

Deadline note: the official scholarship page publishes no exact scholarship deadline. NUS's Important Dates table gives the award's Application Period as 'Based on admissions application timeline'. deadline_date is therefore null and deadline_precision is 'programme_specific'. The concrete dates quoted in typical_application_window are NUS undergraduate ADMISSIONS windows (AY2026/2027 International Qualifications: 3 December 2025 to 23 February 2026; AY2027/2028 International Qualifications except IB Diploma: 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027; IB Diploma: 16 December 2026 to 3 February 2027), not scholarship deadlines.

Status note: as of the verification date the AY2026/2027 cycle is complete (interviews January-July 2026, outcomes by mid-July 2026) and the AY2027/2028 admissions window had not yet opened, so status is 'UPCOMING'. At capture time the NUS Important Dates page displayed '[Closed]' markers against the AY2027/2028 rows even though those windows open on 16 December 2026; this appears to be a page-rendering artefact and is flagged for re-check. NUS's most recent admissions announcement was still the AY2026/2027 exercise.
programme_duration.duration_months (48) is a mechanical conversion of the officially stated maximum of four years; the official source states years only.

official_programme_guide_url is null: no NUS-published rulebook, handbook or policy PDF specific to the 2026-renamed award was located. The award's terms are published on the NUS award page itself, and ABS publishes GKSS FAQs (abs.org.sg/docs/library/) that describe the earlier multi-university arrangement; those historical FAQ PDFs were deliberately not cited as the programme guide because they predate the 2026 renaming and consolidation.
Benefit amounts are those published by NUS for the renamed award in its first cycle (from 2026). Amounts may be revised in future cycles; re-verification is due 2026-12-20.

Compulsory miscellaneous fees (registration, student activity, health service and insurance, and academic-related fees) are NOT covered by this award, and living costs beyond the stated allowances are not covered. Only the tuition fee is listed as covered by NUS.

This award does NOT include the Student Exchange Programme placement or campus-accommodation priority benefits that some sibling NUS scholarships (for example the NUS Global Merit Scholarship and the NUS Undergraduate Scholarship) carry. Those benefits were not claimed for this award.

The record uses the verification date 2026-10-03 mandated by the SCHEMA_CONTRACT. Page crawls were performed during the same working session (early-to-mid October 2026); the date used is the contract's reference date and no material cycle boundary falls between the two.

No logo image is attached (logo_url null, image_url null). This is an honest outcome: no verifiable logo asset URL on nus.edu.sg could be confirmed because of the site's bot protection, and third-party aggregators were rejected per the logo rules.

The English-language requirement field is deliberately sparse. The official scholarship page sets no English test requirement; NUS's admission requirements set English expectations per qualification, and no minimum IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/Duolingo score is attributed to this award.

No age limit, gender restriction or per-country nationality quota is published for this award; those fields are null/false accordingly. ABS's donor page states that 3 to 4 scholarships are awarded each year, which is recorded as an indicative number rather than a formal quota.
